title: Persist CH9329 baudrate across a power cycle
problem: Openterface writes the CH9329's pin-reported serial mode 0x80 back through CMD_SET_PARA_CFG even though the protocol accepts only writable software modes 0x00-0x02. The menu path also discards the command response and resets after an error, so 115200 appears to work until power is removed and reconnect falls back to 9600.
reproduce: Inspect both baudrate parameter packets at the reporter's pinned revision: byte 6 is 0x80. The official WCH protocol identifies 0x80-0x82 as read-only hardware-pin states and limits CMD_SET_PARA_CFG serial mode values to 0x00-0x02.
acceptance: Both 9600 and 115200 parameter packets use writable protocol mode 0x00, and menu, strategy and diagnostics paths accept only a matching successful response with a valid checksum before reset. The baseline check fails and the unchanged check passes on the candidate.
repair: Encode software protocol mode in persistent parameter packets and centralize strict CH9329 response validation across configuration and reset paths.

verification.limitations: BCL proves the invalid baseline packet, writable candidate packet, and strict response gates. A separate Ubuntu 24.04 qmake build compiled the complete application and five focused Qt tests passed. Only the reporter can prove nonvolatile persistence on a physical CH9329 power cycle.
verification.ownerCheck: Start connected at 9600, select 115200, unplug the complete Mini-KVM, reconnect it, and confirm GET_INFO answers at 115200 and the stored baudrate remains 115200.

selection.reason: A fresh CH9329 owner supplied four power-cycle reproductions at an exact current revision, no competing PR exists, and the malformed command is independently verifiable against the official protocol.

negative.outputIncludes: persistent SET_PARA_CFG packets must use software protocol mode 0x00
